# testprune

> testprune is a Claude Code skill that audits a repository's automated test suite, removes the obsolete tests that no longer describe production, retargets the invariants worth keeping at the production code path, and builds layered gates so a routine check finishes in seconds instead of minutes. It ends by writing a test policy into `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` so coding agents stop reaching for the full suite. It runs once against a repository rather than continuously in CI, it never changes production runtime behavior, and every deletion is recoverable from the commit hash it records.

Install by cloning the repository into `~/.claude/skills/testprune`, then invoke it in a Claude Code session opened on the target repository with `/testprune` (audit and execute), `/testprune prompt-first` (write a curated repo-specific prompt and change nothing), or `/testprune followups` (execute high-blast-radius items a prior pass deferred). It produces a layered gate script, corrected and retargeted tests, an updated testing document, a policy block in `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`, a ledger of every deletion with its git recovery hash, and a final report with measured before-and-after numbers.

It is language-agnostic in design and works with any test runner, though the reference examples are Python and pytest, so other stacks require adapting commands rather than concepts. It is not a test impact analysis or predictive test selection service, not a flaky-test detector or quarantine system, not a coverage or mutation-testing tool, and not an implementation of formal test-suite minimization research.

Evidence status: the only measured result published for this skill is a single-repository before-and-after (a 24-minute suite with 186 stale failures became a 10-second fast gate with zero failures and a 10-minute broad gate with 33 classified pre-existing failures). That is one case, not a benchmark. The skill has not been evaluated on SWE-bench or any public benchmark, and no claim is made about its effect on agent regression rates.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuraCerebra-AI/testprune/HEAD/README.md): overview, install, comparison with adjacent tools, FAQ
- [SKILL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuraCerebra-AI/testprune/HEAD/SKILL.md): the rules, the 13-step checklist, the execution model, the safety rules
- [rationale_and_pitfalls.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuraCerebra-AI/testprune/HEAD/references/rationale_and_pitfalls.md): why each rule exists and the failure mode behind it

## Modes

| Mode | What it does | Budget | Changes tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `direct` (default) | Audits the suite, executes low and medium blast-radius changes, builds and measures the gates, writes the policy block and the ledger | Two hours | Yes |
| `prompt-first` | Reads the repository and writes a curated, repo-specific audit prompt plus a companion follow-up prompt | Read-only | No |
| `followups` | Executes the high-blast-radius items a prior pass deferred, adjudicating which claimant is the authority before any test moves | Forty-five minutes | Yes, after adjudication |

Mode definitions: [prompt_creator.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuraCerebra-AI/testprune/HEAD/references/prompt_creator.md) and [followups_execution.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuraCerebra-AI/testprune/HEAD/references/followups_execution.md).

## Components

- [gate_script_template.sh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuraCerebra-AI/testprune/HEAD/references/gate_script_template.sh): the fast, subsystem, broad, and archive gate script, bash 3.2 compatible, runner-agnostic
- [agent_instruction_block.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuraCerebra-AI/testprune/HEAD/references/agent_instruction_block.md): the test policy block written into `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`, in JSON and Markdown forms
- [techniques.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuraCerebra-AI/testprune/HEAD/references/techniques.md): sleep spy for locating a slow test's real wait, measurement commands, zero-paid-call proof, archive move, gitignore allowlist edits, hunk-only staging, registry sweep
- [final_report.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuraCerebra-AI/testprune/HEAD/references/final_report.md): the closing report format, the Done / Optional / Parked structure, and both visualization templates
- [test_inventory.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuraCerebra-AI/testprune/HEAD/scripts/test_inventory.py): reports test modules on disk versus tracked in git versus gitignored but still collected, for pytest, Jest, Vitest, Go, Rust, and Ruby conventions

## Core rules

- Only tests that exercise the production path may certify a change. Deprecated and parallel implementations are named by file and never given tests.
- Permanently red or vacuous tests are deleted with `git rm` (recoverable) or parked in a gitignored archive. Never skip-forever, never a root conftest skip, never xfail-forever.
- A real invariant is retargeted at production before the test carrying it is deleted.
- Tests over rows in a retired format that prove readability, calm refusal, migration, or stored-row contracts are production coverage and stay.
- The fast gate is an explicit file list with zero known failures and runs in seconds.
- Every number comes from tool output, measured before and after.
- No test that claims to be offline may reach a paid, networked, or credentialed service.

## Key facts

- License: MIT
- Platforms: any operating system running Claude Code; requires `git`, `bash` 3.2 or newer, and Python 3.7 or newer for the inventory script
- Install: `git clone https://github.com/NeuraCerebra-AI/testprune.git ~/.claude/skills/testprune`
- Invocation: `/testprune`, `/testprune prompt-first`, `/testprune followups`
- Model invocation: disabled by default (`disable-model-invocation: true`), because the skill deletes tests
- Output: a layered gate script, retargeted tests, an updated testing document, a `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` policy block, a deletion ledger with git recovery hashes, and a measured final report
- Repository: https://github.com/NeuraCerebra-AI/testprune
